definitions.explanation: Preparatory work done before the main task, especially in cooking (washing, cutting, marinating ingredients) but also used more broadly for any advance preparation.

examples.japanese: {野菜|やさい}の{下準備|したじゅんび}をする。
examples.english: Do the prep work for the vegetables.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}の{下準備|したじゅんび}を{前|まえ}の{日|ひ}に{済|す}ませた。
examples.english: I finished the cooking prep the day before.

examples.japanese: イベントの{成功|せいこう}には{十分|じゅうぶん}な{下準備|したじゅんび}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Thorough preparation is indispensable for the success of an event.

notes:
{下準備|したじゅんび} literally means "under-preparation" — the groundwork done before the main task.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下準備|したじゅんび}をする (do prep work)
- {下準備|したじゅんび}を{済|す}ませる (finish the preparation)
- {下準備|したじゅんび}が{大切|たいせつ} (preparation is important)
- {下準備|したじゅんび}に{時間|じかん}がかかる (preparation takes time)

Most commonly used in cooking contexts, where it refers to tasks like washing, peeling, cutting, and marinating ingredients before the actual cooking begins.
